userStories.title: Advance the reviewed head on the bot's own workflow index
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid `head` and `base` SHAs and `listPrComments` returning the bot's own `w-index` comment with `reviewedHead` equal to `expectedHead` and a reviewed pair to update, when `advanceReviewedHead` runs, then it returns `{ kind: "advanced" }`.

Given valid target SHAs and a re-read own `w-index` whose `reviewedHead` matches `expectedHead`, whose reviewed pair differs from the target pair, and which has two keys and one pending reopen, when `advanceReviewedHead` runs, then `_reviewedHeadDeps.editComment` is called exactly once on that re-read comment with the body `withNaxBotMarker(renderItemIndex({ ...fresh, reviewedHead: head, reviewedBase: base }, settled), "w-index")`, where `fresh` is the parsed re-read index and `settled` is its settled count.

Given an own `w-index` with a matching `expectedHead`, a reviewed pair to update, and first index line `nax workflow items: 3 (2 settled)`, when `advanceReviewedHead` runs with valid target SHAs, then the body passed to `editComment` has first index line `nax workflow items: 3 (2 settled)`.

Given an own `w-index` with a matching `expectedHead`, a reviewed pair to update, and legacy first index line `nax workflow open items: 2`, when `advanceReviewedHead` runs with valid target SHAs, then the body passed to `editComment` has first index line `nax workflow items: 2 (0 settled)`.
When the re-read index prints `Reviewed head: none` and `expectedHead` is `undefined`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "advanced" }` for valid target SHAs.
When the fresh index's `reviewedHead` differs from `expectedHead`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "moved" }` without calling `editComment`.

When the re-read index already has `reviewedHead` equal to both `expectedHead` and `head`, and `reviewedBase` equal to `base`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "unchanged" }` without calling `editComment`.

When the re-read finds no own `w-index` comment, including when the only `w-index` comment is authored by a login other than `input.login`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "no-index" }` without calling `editComment`.
When the own `w-index` comment's body does not parse as an index, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "unparseable" }` without calling `editComment`.
When `head` is not a 40-character hex SHA, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "invalid-sha" }` without calling `listPrComments` or `editComment`.
When `base` is not a 40-character hex SHA, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "invalid-sha" }` without calling `listPrComments` or `editComment`.
When `listPrComments` rejects, then `advanceReviewedHead` resolves to `{ kind: "failed" }` without calling `editComment`.
When `editComment` rejects, then `advanceReviewedHead` resolves to `{ kind: "failed" }`.

Given `listPrComments` returning two own `w-index` comments in forge order, older then newer, both with `reviewedHead` matching `expectedHead` and a reviewed pair to update, when `advanceReviewedHead` runs, then it edits the newer comment, not the older one.
When the re-read index has `reviewedHead` equal to both `expectedHead` and `head` but a `reviewedBase` different from `base`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "advanced" }`.
When `expectedHead` is defined and the re-read index prints `Reviewed head: none`, then `advanceReviewedHead` returns `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "moved" }`.
When `parseItemIndexSettled` reads a valid `w-index` body built with `withNaxBotMarker` whose first index line is `nax workflow items: 3 (2 settled)`, then it returns `2`.
When `parseItemIndexSettled` reads a valid `w-index` body built with `withNaxBotMarker` whose first index line is `nax workflow open items: 2`, then it returns `0`.
When `parseItemIndex` rejects a body, then `parseItemIndexSettled` returns `null` for that body.

routing.reasoning: Small additive helper and parser change using existing forge adapters; strict isolation applies because author ownership controls which remote comment the helper may edit.

userStories.title: Advance the workflow index after a complete posted bot review
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire `advanceReviewedHead` into the completed post path of `runBotReview` without changing its result (#2996).

**Motivation** — So every bot re-review after publish covers `publishedHead..HEAD`.

**Approach** — Integration context:
- `reviewRange(input: { index?: ItemIndex; checkout: PrCheckout; head: string }, isAncestor): Promise<{ rangeBase: string; conversationOnly?: boolean }>` and `reviewScopeOf(...)`: `BotReviewScope` (`"full" | "incremental" | "conversation-only"`) in `packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts`. `reviewRange` returns `conversationOnly: true` when `reviewedHead === head`. This requires valid stored SHAs and both ancestry checks to pass; `input.full` bypasses range narrowing.
- `readReviewRulings(...)` returns `reviewedIndex?: ItemIndex`. It is the index parsed from the bot's own `w-index` comment at preparation time. It is `undefined` when the PR body has no `<!-- nax-workflow:v1 -->` marker, when the PR is untrusted (`staticMode`), when there is no parseable index, or when the ruling read throws.
- `PostReviewOutcome { earlierAnswered; inlineFindings; threadsAnswered; commentsAnswered; offLine; failed }` in `packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts`. `failed` counts forge writes that did not land.
- `PrCheckout.mergeBase`: the merge base the review diffed against.

`runBotReview` calls `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` only when all of these hold. They mirror the publish rule in `reviewedIndex`: the review ran, nothing was left unread, and nothing was cut short.

- the post step produced a `PostReviewOutcome` and its `failed` is `0` (thread and earlier-reply writes; a finding that could not be placed inline goes to the summary as off-line and does not count);
- the review reported no unread files;
- `readReviewRulings` returned a `reviewedIndex` (so the PR is trusted, marked, and has a parseable index);
- the review scope is not `conversation-only`.

`input.full` does not change the rule: a full review covers the whole range, so it advances too. The call passes `expectedHead = env.reviewedIndex.reviewedHead`, `head = info.headSha`, `base = checkout.mergeBase`, `login = env.login`, the PR ref, `_botReviewDeps.forge` and the repository root. `runBotReview` returns the same `BotReviewResult` whatever the advance returns. `executeReview` does not wrap the call in its own guard: `advanceReviewedHead` resolves for every failure and never rejects (US-001). This rules out a redundant error-catching wrapper, not the eligibility checks above.

Why `base = checkout.mergeBase`: `reviewRange` accepts the stored base only when it is an ancestor of the next review's merge base. The current merge base is what this review actually diffed against, so the next review's check is exact.

- `packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-review.ts` — `makeBotReviewDeps` stubs `_botReviewDeps` member by member. Without a stub, the new default `advanceReviewedHead` would call the real forge (`gh`) from every `runBotReview` test whose stubbed ruling outcome carries an index (the incremental, lineage, coverage-record, scope and finding-rulings integration tests). The helper gains `advanceReviewedHead: async () => ({ kind: "unchanged" })`. No assertion changes.
- US-002 calls US-001's `advanceReviewedHead` through `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` from `runBotReview`, the function both `nax bot review` and the `nax bot fix` re-review call. Its seam ACs trigger `runBotReview` with the dependency stubbed, entering above the call conditions.

**Scope** — In: the dependency and environment wiring, the post-completion call, the shared test stub, and `runBotReview` integration tests. Out: implementing the comment writer and settled-count reader (US-001); adding a writer to `nax bot fix`, its readiness pass or `nax workflow record` / `promote`; finding provenance for bot fix agents or routing fix-induced chains to the advisor; extending incremental review to unmarked PRs; changing publish or `refreshIndex`; exposing the advance outcome in the result, artifact, or summary. A qualifying posted review invoked by the fix cycle uses the same review hook, not a separate fix writer.

**Interface**
- `_botReviewDeps` (defined in `packages/nax/src/bot/review-deps.ts`, re-exported from `review-run.ts`). Baseline: no index write after the post step. Target: gains `advanceReviewedHead: typeof advanceReviewedHead`, defaulting to the new function (US-002).
- `ReviewEnv` (`review-run.ts`, not exported). Baseline: `{ cost, ctx, review, post }` plus the preparation fields; the `reviewedIndex` that `readReviewRulings` returns stays local to `reviewEnvironment`. Target: gains `reviewedIndex?: ItemIndex` (the index as read at preparation) and `login: string` (the bot login, `items.login`), set by `reviewEnvironment` (US-002).
- `runBotReview` / `executeReview` (`review-run.ts`). Baseline: returns after the step graph posts. Target: when the post step produced a `PostReviewOutcome`, `executeReview` calls `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` once under the conditions in Approach, before it returns the result. It reads `state.posted`, `state.unreadFiles`, `env.post.scope`, `env.reviewedIndex`, `env.login`, `env.review.mergeBase`, `env.post.info.headSha`, `env.post.ref` and `env.post.cwd`. The `BotReviewResult` shape is unchanged (US-002).
acceptanceCriteria: Given a trusted workflow-marked PR, a `recordPrRulings` index with `reviewedHead` A and a valid `reviewedBase`, `isAncestor` returning true, a distinct PR head C, no unread files, and a post outcome with `failed: 0`, when `runBotReview` runs, then it calls the stubbed `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` exactly once after `postPrReview` resolves.

Given the qualifying review of head C from index head A, when `runBotReview` calls `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`, then its input has `expectedHead` A, `head` C, `base` equal to the checkout's `mergeBase`, and `login` equal to the bot login returned by `readCurrentUser`.

Given the qualifying review of head C from index head A, when `runBotReview` calls `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`, then its input carries the resolved PR `ref`, the repository root as `cwd`, and the same `_botReviewDeps.forge` object as `deps`.
Given the same qualifying review setup with `input.full` set to `true`, when `runBotReview` runs, then it calls the stubbed `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` once with `head` C.
When an otherwise qualifying review posts with `failed > 0`, including `failed: 1`, then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.
When `runPrReview` returns `ran: true` with a non-empty `unreadFiles` list for an otherwise qualifying post, then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.

Given no full-review override, valid stored SHAs that pass both ancestry checks, and a PR head equal to the index's `reviewedHead` (a conversation-only review), when `runBotReview` posts with `failed: 0` and no unread files, then it does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.
When `runPrReview` returns `ran: false`, then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.
When the PR body lacks the `<!-- nax-workflow:v1 -->` marker, then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.
When the PR is classified untrusted (static mode), then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.
When `recordPrRulings` returns an outcome with no `index`, then `runBotReview` does not call `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead`.

When `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` resolves to `{ kind: "failed" }` after a qualifying post, then `runBotReview` resolves with `outcome: "posted"` and the same result as if the advance had succeeded.

When `_botReviewDeps.advanceReviewedHead` resolves to `{ kind: "skipped", reason: "moved" }` after a qualifying post, then `runBotReview` resolves with `outcome: "posted"` and the same result as if the advance had succeeded.

routing.reasoning: Localized post-run wiring can be tested through the existing dependency stub; it consumes provenance already gated by readReviewRulings without implementing new trust or permission checks.

modifiedFiles.reason: `makeBotReviewDeps` stubs `_botReviewDeps` member by member. Without a stub, the new default `advanceReviewedHead` would call the real forge (`gh`) from every `runBotReview` test whose stubbed ruling outcome carries an index (the incremental, lineage, coverage-record, scope and finding-rulings integration tests). The helper gains `advanceReviewedHead: async () => ({ kind: "unchanged" })`. No assertion changes.

analysis:
Goal (#2996): after a complete posted bot review of a workflow PR, use that review's head rather than the publish head as the starting point for the next eligible incremental review. This reduces repeated review of earlier fix pushes; it does not solve fix-chain provenance or guarantee convergence. This is a TypeScript/Bun enhancement contained in packages/nax. The graph navigation tool was unavailable, so the baseline was verified with direct source reads and text search.

Existing range and provenance: packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts:122 obtains reviewedIndex from the ruling recorder only for a trusted, workflow-marked PR; absent or failed reads leave it undefined. packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts:192 classifies full, incremental, and conversation-only; packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts:203 checks the stored head against the current head and the stored base against the current checkout merge base. Valid same-head provenance yields conversation-only; invalid or unverifiable provenance falls back to the merge base. A successful advance is used by this existing reader on the next run, so neither its algorithm nor the CLI needs changing. The stored base must be the actual checkout merge base, not the PR base SHA or the incremental starting head.

US-001 source impact: add the helper and unit tests, and add a settled-count export to the existing packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads.ts:260 (the spec's Modifies list refers to existing test assertions; the existing source file must still be edited). ItemIndex at packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads.ts:21 does not contain the count; packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads.ts:248 renders it separately. packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads.ts:101 normalizes raw and marked comment bodies and handles CRLF. The new reader must agree with the entire existing parser, including count consistency and pending-reopen validation, not just recognize a header. Do not change ItemIndex or parseItemIndex behavior. packages/nax/src/workflow/item-thread-state.ts:65 distinguishes the selected comment from its parse result; it takes the last matching own comment in forge order and does not fall back to an older valid body. packages/nax/src/forge/marker.ts:27 matches exact author login and parses the marker, preserving input order. Reuse those ownership semantics; a marker alone never confers ownership. The forge barrel exposes the list, marker, and edit adapters at packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:23, packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:56, and packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:77. packages/nax/src/forge/threads.ts:300 supplies forge comments in endpoint/page order; packages/nax/src/forge/comments.ts:271 edits the supplied comment on GitHub or GitLab and may reject. Validate exactly 40 hexadecimal characters before calling the forge; packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads.ts:244 demonstrates full-match validation that rejects a trailing newline. Compare exact head values before the unchanged check: an observed change wins even if it already landed the desired pair; if the head did not move, a base-only change can be corrected. Render from the fresh index and settled count, not a preparation snapshot. The write is best-effort, introduces one fresh read and at most one edit per qualifying run, and has no forge-side compare-and-swap. Changes to keys, pending reopens, or settled count already present at re-read time are retained; a writer landing after the re-read may still be overwritten. A skip or failure does not update the marker through this attempt, so the next review uses whatever valid provenance remains and may review a wider range.

US-001 downstream and regression surface: packages/nax/src/bot/rulings.ts:234 re-renders its current index for the settled count without changing reviewed provenance. Workflow publishing uses packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-index.ts:26 and packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-index.ts:96; workflow live status and promotion use the same item-thread reader at packages/nax/src/workflow/live-status.ts:78 and packages/nax/src/workflow/promote-rulings.ts:83. Keep these consumers unchanged. Existing bun:test coverage includes modern/legacy parsing, marked bodies, pending reopens, and count validation at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/item-threads.test.ts:154 and packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/item-threads.test.ts:209; publish provenance and preservation at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/item-threads-reopen.test.ts:275; and marked ruling fixtures and settled-count updates at packages/nax/test/unit/bot/rulings.test.ts:65 and packages/nax/test/unit/bot/rulings.test.ts:292. Stub and restore the new helper's forge dependencies in the unit suite. Use separate valid fixtures for the two-key/pending-reopen edit and the three-key `(2 settled)` preservation case.

US-002 source impact: extend the existing injection object at packages/nax/src/bot/review-deps.ts:32 (re-exported at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:38), and the private ReviewEnv at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:89. Preparation already has the triaged bot login and reviewed index at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:291 and packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:323; it computes range and scope at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:358 and supplies post cwd from repoRoot. The graph at packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:132 records unreadFiles and only enters the post step when reviewRan is true; the post node awaits posting before producing state.posted. Put the single awaited advance after successful graph completion and the existing not-reviewed guard in executeReview (packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:429), not inside preparation, the graph's review node, or postPrReview. Undefined and empty unreadFiles both mean no unread files. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:541 computes failed from thread and earlier-reply failures; offLine is tracked separately. Do not treat offLine findings, intent, or quality as extra gates, and do not change how postPrReview handles its existing artifact, summary, or coverage record. The existing preparation provenance is the trust gate for this new mutation; no new trust classifier or credential handling is needed. The helper contains forge failures, so its return value is not merged into the result or persisted. Preserve BotReviewResult, including existing log path and metrics behavior. The CLI at packages/nax/src/cli/bot.ts:126 and the fix cycle's actual re-review at packages/nax/src/bot/fix-cycle.ts:54 share the service; a qualifying posted re-review can advance through the same hook, but the fix/readiness path adds no writer of its own.

US-002 tests: packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-incremental.test.ts:49 provides the dependency setup and restore pattern; packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-incremental.test.ts:96 provides unmarked/fork fallbacks. Use distinct reviewed head, reviewed base, PR head, and checkout merge-base SHA fixtures for provenance assertions; packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-review.ts:29 currently uses the placeholder `merge`, so override the checkout locally if needed. Override the shared no-op advance stub with the per-test spy after spreading makeBotReviewDeps. Add that shared no-op at packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-review.ts:8 so incremental, scope, lineage, coverage-record and finding-rulings tests do not call the real forge. Representative consumers are packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-scope.test.ts:78, packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-lineage.test.ts:176, packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-coverage-record.test.ts:86, and packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-finding-rulings.test.ts:103. No existing assertions or graph transitions need replacement.

Compatibility and rollout: land US-001 first (no runtime caller), then US-002. No data migration, backfill, config, cross-package dependency, or CLI flag is needed. Existing parseable indexes can be advanced in place after the next qualifying post; legacy first lines remain readable and are normalized to the modern format with zero settled only on an actual edit. PRs with no usable preparation index are not given a new index by this feature. Workflow republish and ruling refresh retain their existing behavior.
outOfScope: Making the comment edit conditional at the forge: GitHub and GitLab comment edits have no compare-and-swap. A write that lands between the re-read and the edit can still be overwritten, and the window is one forge round trip.
Advancing the reviewed head from `nax bot fix`, its readiness pass or `nax workflow record` / `promote`: only a posted bot review advances it.
Reviewing PRs without the `<!-- nax-workflow:v1 -->` body marker incrementally: they have no index, so every bot review on them stays a full review (#2996 "Not covered").
Changing the workflow publish rule (`reviewedIndex` / `maintainItemIndex`): a re-publish still writes its own run head.
Reporting the advance outcome in `BotReviewResult`, the bot review artifact or the summary comment; it is logged only.
Finding provenance for bot fix agents and routing fix-induced chains to the advisor (#2987).
Changing `refreshIndex` in `packages/nax/src/bot/rulings.ts`; it keeps re-rendering the index it read.

Coordinating two overlapping index writers (two concurrent `nax bot review` runs on one PR, or a bot review overlapping a workflow re-publish): the later advance sees a changed `reviewedHead` and returns `moved` without writing, and the next review falls back to the wider range.
